recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5950 unless a future work-group decision changes the established Timing.code or Timing.code.text approach.
issue_request: FHIR-5950 requested a human text or coded representation for Timing so institution-specific mnemonic timing patterns could be exchanged alongside the computational timing form; the accepted resolution was to add a CodeableConcept element.
initial_application: The git-svn history contains a direct implementation commit, a4cda65a856e75aae09758faef7d4c91cf3d5ec7, with subject '#5950 - add Timing.code'. It added Timing.code as a 0..1 CodeableConcept in source/datatypes/timing.xml with a TimingAbbreviation binding and explanatory definition text.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Timing as an active datatype and marks it normative. Later same-family work, especially FHIR-13941, preserved the model by documenting free-text timing as Timing.code.text rather than adding another Timing element; that issue already has a combined-branch audit commit. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made because current build-scope source already defines Timing.code as the requested optional CodeableConcept and the Timing narrative explains text in Timing.code.text plus coded Timing.code interpretation.

related_jiras.note: Later Published request for Timing.text was resolved by documenting Timing.code.text on the element added for FHIR-5950; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Mentioned in the seed as broader Timing datatype preparation, but not needed to decide whether the text/coded representation element is present now.
